raw_case_text:
A 36-year-old gravida 2 para 1 woman at 30 weeks' gestation presented to our hospital with complaints of fever, productive cough and cyanosis of 2 days duration. She was recently diagnosed as MB leprosy as evidenced by hypoaesthetic annular plaques on trunk and limbs (Fig. 1), positive slit skin smear (morphological index of 3.2% and bacteriological index (BI) of 4.3). Standard MB-MDT consisting of clofazimine, rifampicin and dapsone (100 mg once daily) was commenced 2 weeks prior to such complaints. She had no complaints of headache, chest pain, palpitation, dyspnea, altered consciousness, hemoptysis or syncope. She denied any exposure to chemicals or unprescribed medications.
On examination, she had central cyanosis and one spike of fever on admission. Apart from low oxygen saturation (SpO2 = 84-88%), her vital signs were stable with no evidence of respiratory distress. Radial artery and venous blood was dark-colored. Arterial blood gas (ABG) analysis under room air showed PO2 of 111 mmHg and SO2 of 98 mmHg. There was no laboratory evidence of hemolysis with normal hemoglobin, bilirubin and LDH. Leukocyte count was 7.0 x 103/muL. Sputum workup for culture and acid-fast bacilli (AFB) as well as chest X-ray did not reveal any evidence of lung infection. She was not G6PD deficient.
Patient was administered 100% oxygen inhalation, but there was no improvement in cyanosis (Fig. 2) and SpO2 by pulse oximetry remained around 85%. Repeated ABG revealed almost similar values. Three pairs of intravenous (IV) parentrovite, which contained 1500 mg of ascorbic acid were given at the initial suspicion of methaemoglobinemia. Oral vitamin C (1000 mg/day) was also prescribed. As for MDT leprosy treatment, dapsone was replaced by ofloxacin 200 mg twice daily and patient was closely monitored thereafter. There was a gradual increase in SpO2 level with value of 90% 2 days later and 99% after 1 week. No cyanosis was evident, and there was a change in color of venous blood by this time. She delivered a healthy baby via spontaneous vaginal delivery 9 weeks later.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 36-year-old pregnant woman (gravida 2, para 1) at 30 weeks' gestation presented with a 2-day history of fever, productive cough, and central cyanosis 2 weeks after starting multibacillary leprosy multidrug therapy.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Two weeks prior to admission, the patient was diagnosed with multibacillary leprosy (based on hypoesthetic annular truncal/limb plaques and a positive slit-skin smear showing a Bacteriological Index of 4.3 and Morphological Index of 3.2%) and initiated on standard WHO multibacillary multidrug therapy consisting of rifampicin, clofazimine, and dapsone 100 mg once daily. Two days before presentation, she developed fever, productive cough, and progressive bluish discoloration of the lips and mucosa without dyspnea.
subjective.past_medical_history: Gravida 2, para 1 at 30 weeks' gestation; recently diagnosed with multibacillary leprosy 2 weeks prior; denied chemical exposures or unprescribed medications.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever, productive cough, and cyanosis; negative for headache, chest pain, palpitations, dyspnea, altered sensorium, hemoptysis, or syncope.

objective.physical_examination: The patient had central cyanosis, hypoesthetic annular plaques on the trunk and extremities, a single febrile spike on admission, and pulse oximetry oxygen saturation (SpO2) of 84-88% on room air (remaining ~85% despite 100% oxygen inhalation), with otherwise stable vital signs and no respiratory distress.
objective.routine_investigations: Drawn radial arterial and venous blood appeared dark chocolate-brown. Room-air arterial blood gas (ABG) showed PaO2 111 mmHg and calculated SaO2 98% (demonstrating a marked saturation gap). Complete blood count and hemolysis workup showed normal hemoglobin, normal bilirubin, normal LDH, WBC 7.0 x 10^3/uL, and normal G6PD activity. Sputum AFB smear and culture and chest radiograph were negative for pulmonary infection.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Based on central cyanosis unresponsive to 100% oxygen, dark chocolate-brown blood, and a wide pulse-oximetry-to-ABG oxygen saturation gap (SpO2 84-88% vs. PaO2 111 mmHg/SaO2 98%) without hemolysis, a diagnosis of dapsone-induced methemoglobinemia complicating multibacillary leprosy in pregnancy was established. Dapsone was immediately discontinued and replaced with oral ofloxacin 200 mg twice daily alongside three pairs of intravenous Parentrovite (containing 1,500 mg ascorbic acid) and oral vitamin C 1,000 mg/day; SpO2 rose to 90% within 2 days and 99% at 1 week with complete resolution of cyanosis, and she delivered a healthy infant vaginally 9 weeks later.
